hook: Gillian Hadfield is the Bloomberg Distinguished Professor of AI Alignment and Governance at Johns Hopkins University, with appointments in the School of Government and Policy and the Whiting School of Engineering, according to the university. Johns Hopkins says she introduced the regulatory markets idea in her book Rules for a Flat World and applied it to AI safety with Jack Clark in 2019. The university describes the independent verification organization (IVO) model, now in California law through SB 813, as the current form of that idea. In September 2026 Governor Gavin Newsom named her one of four experts advising California on AI safety.

quick_facts: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor of AI Alignment and Governance at Johns Hopkins University, with appointments in the School of Government and Policy and the Whiting School of Engineering, and an affiliation with the university's Data Science and AI Institute, according to Johns Hopkins (the Hub, October 30, 2026)
Johns Hopkins announced the Bloomberg Distinguished Professorship on June 26, 2025, according to the university's announcement of that date
Her appointment at Johns Hopkins began in July 2024, as Professor of Government and Policy and Professor of Computer Science, according to her LinkedIn profile

Senior advisor to Fathom, a nonprofit that works on independent oversight of AI, as Fathom's release on California's report of November 18, 2026 describes her; her LinkedIn profile does not list the role
Member of Fathom's Executive Council, which Fathom announced on October 29, 2026
One of four experts Governor Gavin Newsom named on September 23, 2026 to advise California on AI safety under his executive order, according to the Governor's office
Named to Canada's National Council on Artificial Intelligence, which advises Prime Minister Mark Carney, according to Johns Hopkins

At the University of Toronto from July 2018 to July 2024 as Professor of Law and Professor of Strategic Management, Schwartz Reisman Chair in Technology and Society from June 2019, and director of the Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society from July 2019 to June 2024, per her LinkedIn profile
Faculty member at the Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence since May 2022, per her LinkedIn profile
Senior Policy Advisor at OpenAI from August 2018 to June 2024, per her LinkedIn profile
Kirtland Professor of Law and Professor of Economics at the University of Southern California from 2001 to 2018, per her LinkedIn profile
Holds a JD and a PhD in economics from Stanford University and a BA (Honours) in economics from Queen's University, per her LinkedIn profile

achievements.title: Regulatory markets
achievements.impact: Governments set the level of risk that is acceptable and license private actors who can show a system stays within it. Johns Hopkins says she introduced the idea in Rules for a Flat World and applied it to AI safety with Jack Clark in 2019, and that independent verification organizations are the version in current proposals.

achievements.title: Rules for a Flat World
achievements.impact: Her book, subtitled Why Humans Invented Law and How to Reinvent It for a Complex Global Economy. Her LinkedIn profile gives Oxford University Press, 2017, with a new edition in 2020; Johns Hopkins dates the book to 2016.

achievements.title: Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society
achievements.impact: Directed the University of Toronto institute from July 2019 to June 2024 and held the Schwartz Reisman Chair in Technology and Society, per her LinkedIn profile.

The July 2024 start at Johns Hopkins is from LinkedIn and the Bloomberg Distinguished Professorship, announced June 26, 2025, is from Johns Hopkins; they are two facts with two sources.
